entities.summary:
Abu al-Hasan al-Tabari (abu-al-hasan-al-tabari): A 10th-century Persian physician from Tabaristan, Abu al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Tabari was born in Amol, Iran, in 955 CE. He was the physician of Rukn al-Dawla, a Buyid ruler, and served during the reign of the Samanid Empire. Al-Tabari's work is notable for its contributions to the field of medicine, particularly in the area of pharmacology.






Al-Tabari's legacy extends beyond his medical contributions, as he played a significant role in the transmission of knowledge from the Islamic Golden Age to the medieval world. His writings on medicine and philosophy were widely studied and influential in the development of European medicine during the Middle Ages.





Al-Tabari's significance lies in his ability to bridge the cultural and intellectual divides between East and West, making him a crucial figure in the transmission of knowledge between the ancient and medieval worlds.
